label: Vireo Valley, symptom 'hard_fault'
headline: Vireo Valley's 3.6x hard-fault rate is not an inverter problem — five of eight events are MV collector cable and switchgear terminations across three blocks, including two cable faults at the same run position on different circuits, and the site's inverter fault rate is at fleet baseline once those are removed.
action: Commission VLF tan-delta and partial-discharge testing plus a termination/splice audit on the Vireo Valley MV collector circuits serving B01, B03 and B04 and the main feeder, and pull the EPC construction records for those pulls to establish whether the terminations fall under the original installation warranty.
reasoning: Five of the eight members are MV collector/switchgear events (WO-2024-00060, WO-2025-00298, WO-2025-00317, WO-2025-00705, WO-2025-00837) spanning blocks B01, B03, B04 and the main feeder, with physical evidence of termination workmanship: an MV termination kit x3 consumed on WO-2025-00317, a failed switchgear termination replaced on WO-2025-00837, and two independent cable faults located at roughly the same run position (~300 ft in from the block end) on different circuits — H1's discriminating signature. Stripping the MV/conductor WOs leaves only three inverter-level faults (WO-2024-00188 string self-stop, WO-2025-00351 OEM warranty control board, WO-2025-00614 gate driver) over 3.5 GW-months, i.e. essentially the fleet baseline of 0.63/GW-month, which is what H4 and H3 would have to explain away and cannot. H2 has real support — WO-2025-00298 and WO-2025-00317 are near-identical four days apart — but the controls show the same boilerplate reuse fleet-wide (WO-2024-00188 at Vireo is textually the same event write-up as control WO-2025-00695 at Sandhill Bend; controls WO-2026-00049 and WO-2025-00882 are the same DC-GF template at two different sites; WO-2026-00030 and WO-2025-00320 are the same PM template), so templating is a corpus-wide style, not a Vireo-specific inflation mechanism, and even collapsing that one pair leaves four MV events on three separate blocks. The control set contains no MV collector or switchgear faults at any comparison site — every non-Vireo control is DC-side, inverter thermal, or PM — which is the strongest argument that the MV concentration is local to Vireo rather than an artifact of how faults are coded.
contradicting: WO-2025-00298 and WO-2025-00317 are near-identical narratives four days apart and may be one event double-booked, which would cut the MV count from 5 to 4; WO-2024-00060 and WO-2025-00705 are also near-identical text (a year apart, different techs), so at least part of the cluster's coherence is narrative templating rather than confirmed distinct events. Exposure is only 3.5 GW-months, so the Poisson interval on a lift of 3.65 is wide. Both April 2025 cable faults are still 'pending' with contractors scheduled, so no confirmed root cause has been returned, and the recurring overnight feeder trips (WO-2024-00060, WO-2025-00705) explicitly closed with 'no root cause established' — they could be a grid-side or relay-setting issue rather than a cable defect.

population_detail.description: MV collector circuits at Vireo Valley implicated by member narratives: block feeders B01, B03, B04, plus the main feeder / switchgear bus. Inverter installed-base tables (KVP-3600, MG-3300) are not the exposed population here — the residual inverter fault rate at this site is at baseline.
population_detail.basis: Count of distinct circuit/block identifiers named in cluster narratives: B01 (WO-2025-00298), B03 (WO-2025-00317), B04 (WO-2025-00837), main feeder (WO-2024-00060, WO-2025-00705). Total MV circuit length and splice count at the site are not quantifiable from this data.

hypotheses.statement: Vireo Valley has a real, localized MV collector defect (bad cable terminations/splices from a single installation campaign) that produces feeder relay trips and cable faults, and this accounts for most of the site's hard_fault excess.
predictions: At least half of Vireo hard_fault WOs carry component in {mv_equipment, conductor_or_connector} and mention feeder/collector/switchgear/termination, versus a much lower MV share of hard_fault WOs fleet-wide
Parts consumption at Vireo is skewed to MV termination/splice kits, with repeat purchases across multiple blocks (B01, B03, B04) rather than one block
Repeat WOs on the same feeder or block within 6-12 months (recurrence flags or same asset_id/block string appearing more than once)
Higher-than-fleet share of VENDOR-REFERRED / ESCALATED resolution codes and contractor-scheduled pending outcomes at this site
Inverter-level hard_faults (string/central/gate_driver) at Vireo occur at roughly fleet rate once MV WOs are excluded
discriminating_evidence: Strip all mv_equipment/conductor WOs from the count: if the residual Vireo hard_fault rate falls to ~fleet baseline, the excess is MV-specific (supports H1 over H3/H4)
Fault-location detail: two or more independent WOs reporting a fault distance clustered near the same run position on different circuits indicates a common construction/pulling practice, not chance
Check whether sister sites built by the same EPC/commissioning year also show elevated MV hard_fault rates; a shared build cohort supports systemic defect

hypotheses.statement: The cluster is inflated by duplicate or copy-paste/templated work orders, so the true count of distinct hard_fault events at Vireo Valley is materially fewer than 8.
predictions: Near-identical narrative pairs exist in the set (e.g. the 'site tripped overnight / relay targets pointed at the main feeder / restored under supervision' pair, and the two 'locator put it about 300 ft in' MV cable faults 4 days apart) with matching or repeated labor_hours values (14.5 h appears twice)
Duplicated pairs share tech ID, resolution code, or fall within a few days of each other, or are a re-open/child WO of the same event
Reported lost_mwh or labor hours are duplicated across the pair rather than summing to plausible independent outages
After exact/fuzzy narrative dedupe, n drops (e.g. to 5-6) and rate_per_gw_month falls toward 1.4-1.7 with lift near 2 or below
discriminating_evidence: Run text similarity (>0.85) and same-event linkage checks across the 8 WOs; if two or more collapse, recompute lift and see whether the site still clears the fleet baseline
Compare SCADA/outage timestamps or relay trip events to WO count: if there are fewer distinct trip events than WOs, duplication is confirmed
If duplicated narratives also appear across other sites (shared boilerplate text), the problem is template reuse, not Vireo-specific failure

hypotheses.statement: Vireo Valley technicians label events as 'hard_fault' that crews at other sites label 'offline', 'comms_loss', or 'trip', so the site's total fault burden is normal and only the symptom mix is shifted.
predictions: Vireo's all-symptom CM/Emergency WO rate per GW-month is at or near the fleet mean even though hard_fault is 3.6x
Vireo shows a deficit in other symptom categories (offline/no_output/comms/nuisance_trip) relative to fleet proportions
The hard_fault WOs concentrate among a few tech IDs (TECH-0166 and TECH-0229 each appear twice in a sample of 8); those techs' hard_fault share is elevated at any site they work
A high fraction of Vireo 'hard_fault' WOs resolve with RESET only and no parts, i.e. severity does not match the label
discriminating_evidence: Compute per-tech symptom mix across all sites: if the same techs over-code hard_fault elsewhere too, it is a labeling habit, not a site defect
Compare Vireo total WO rate and total lost_mwh per GW-month to fleet: normal totals with abnormal symptom mix favors H3 over H1
Check whether the sample's low-severity events (string inverter self-stop cleared by restart) are coded as lesser symptoms at other sites

hypotheses.statement: With only 3.5 GW-months of exposure, 8 mechanistically unrelated failures (MV cable, switchgear termination, gate driver, OEM warranty control board, string inverter self-stop) is ordinary Poisson variation plus one seasonal sub-burst, not a coherent pattern.
predictions: Component field is highly heterogeneous: no single component accounts for a majority once duplicates are removed; failure modes do not share an OEM, model prefix (KVP36 vs MGX33), or block
Three of the events fall in a single 15-day window in April 2025; other months at Vireo are at or below fleet rate, so the annualized rate excluding that window is unremarkable
Similar or larger single-site lifts appear at other low-exposure sites in the fleet when the same threshold is applied (look-elsewhere effect)
No recurrence flags and mostly 'resolved' outcomes; mean labor_hours and lost_mwh per WO at Vireo are within fleet interquartile range
discriminating_evidence: Rank all sites by hard_fault lift with exposure-weighted (Poisson) confidence intervals: if Vireo's lower CI bound crosses 1.0 or several comparable-exposure sites show similar lift, the signal is noise
Time-window test: recompute the rate excluding April 2025; if it drops to baseline, the excess is one burst (check for a storm/lightning or grid-event date in that window across neighboring sites)
Persistence test: hard_fault WOs in the 6 months after the candidate window - continued elevation supports H1, reversion to baseline supports H4

exposure_note: Priced at the cost model's inverter replacement rate. This population is not inverters, so treat the count as the reliable figure and this dollar value as indicative only.
